bullets.title: The River Runner
bullets.note: ([Netflix](https://www.netflix.com/title/81457001), [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/River-Runner-4K-UHD/dp/B09GM8D22N/ref=sr_1_1?keywords=the+river+runner&qid=1645540723&sr=8-1), [more options](https://geni.us/TheRiverRunner)). This jumped to the top of my to-watch list, thanks to [Brad Ludden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Ludden) of [First Descents](https://firstdescents.org/), a world-class waterman in his own right and associate producer on this film. [Here’s the trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CdLovewceng). Kudos to director [Rush Sturges](https://riverroots.com/team/rush-sturges) ([@rushsturges](http://instagram.com/rushsturges)), writers [Thayer Walker](http://thayerwalker.com/) ([@inkdwell](http://www.instagram.com/inkdwell)), [Corinna Halloran](https://www.corinnahalloran.com/index) ([@corinnahalloran](https://twitter.com/corinnahalloran)), and the whole team. This _Outside_ feature by Thayer and [Scott Lindgren](https://www.instagram.com/scottlindgren_/?hl=en), the documentary’s protagonist, became a model for the film: “[After a Hard Diagnosis, One Athlete Learns to Soften Up](https://www.outsideonline.com/outdoor-adventure/water-activities/scott-lindgren-kayaker/).”

bullets.title: The Lessons of History
bullets.creator: Will and Ariel Durant
bullets.note: This short and powerful book was first recommended to me by [investor Ray Dalio](https://tim.blog/2017/09/13/ray-dalio/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf). At fewer than 150 pages, it can be digested in a few sittings and offers an impressive overview of human nature and the rise and fall of civilizations. The prose is also beautiful. Here’s the official book description: “A concise survey of the culture and civilization of mankind, _The Lessons of History_ is the result of a lifetime of research from Pulitzer Prize–winning historians Will and Ariel Durant. With their accessible compendium of philosophy and social progress, the Durants take us on a journey through history, exploring the possibilities and limitations of humanity over time.”
